newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-Eurobourses down, French strike hits franc.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Eurobourses down, French strike hits franc.

text.p: European bourses fell on Wednesday with French stocks and the franc suffering from worries that a French truckers strike could spread and damage the economy.
The dollar, meanwhile, strengthened about half a yen after a Bank of Japan report on manufacturing pointed to no increases in interest rates, helping to support the American currency.
French shares fell in early trading on profit-taking after recent peaks and with investors increasingly anxious over the nationwide truckers protest, now in its 10th day.
The blue-chip CAC-40 index was down 0.4 percent.
The dispute also hit the franc, which weakened to 3.3926 marks in initial currency dealings but picked up slightly after the truckers reported progress in marathon negotiations.

The giant Force Ouvriere union said progress had been made toward a deal on retirement at 55 instead of 60, one of three key points of contention in the most serious labour unrest to hit France this year.

But the union also vowed to tighten their stranglehold on the French economy to make employers do more to end the strike and this muted market optimism. The franc was languishing at 3.3882 to the mark by mid-morning.
In London, Europe's biggest bourse, stocks were down slightly in slack trading as investors digested the interest rate implications from the tax measures of Tuesday's budget.
"It looks like we'll be unsettled today as people work out where they want to be in this market," said one trader.

"We had such a good run up ahead of the budget that I think we're going to be disappointed today," said another. "Coupled with the fact that Wall St was actually down last night for the first time in ages I think we'll open easier and cautiously."
Strategists said that finance minister Kenneth Clarke's budget was conservative but not tight enough to allay pressure for further higher intererest rates.
Attention was also diverted to events in New York where the Dow Jones industrials Average finished 20 points down in the wake of its record-breaking run of recent days.

In Frankfurt, the bourse was also down after its record close on Tuesday. Carmaker Volkswagen AG tumbled about five percent after a U.S. judge denied VW's motion to dismiss racketeering claims by rival Opel.

The dollar strengthened on the BOJ's quarterly tankan report which showed the index for big manufacturers rose to minus three from minus seven in August, suggesting no changes in Japanese interest rates.

"The tankan points to no major changes in Japanese interest rates in the near or medium term. That is undermining the yen and supporting sterling and the dollar," said a senior dealer at a Japanese bank.
While in line with expectations, markets were disappointed with the report because ahead of publication Japanese officials had been sounding upbeat on the economy.

"There is enough in this survey to confirm that the recovery continues...But it is perhaps less positive than I would have liked with interest rates on hold for the forseeable future," said Daiwa Europe economist Julian Fisher.
On bullion markets, platinum was fixed at $377.75 an ounce, the lowest since December 8, 1993, amid bearish market sentiment across the precious metals complex.
Its sister metal palladium was also set lower, fixing at $114.75 an ounce, the lowest since April 20, 1993.
CURRENCIES AT 1020 GMT
The dollar was quoted at 113.20 yen and 1.5247 marks against 112.65 yen and 1.5251 marks late on Tuesday.
STOCK MARKETS AT 1020 GMT
The FTSE 100 index of leading British shares down 4.2 points at 4,064.2.
In Paris, the CAC-40 share index was down 8.05 points at 2,267.03.
The 30-share DAX index in Frankfurt was down 9.09 at 2801.55.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold fixed slightly higher at $373.95 vs $373.50 on Tuesday afternoon and London's close of $373.75. Silver was up one cent at $4.76.
